system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at 20% of price (A$4.8m). | Higher cap (at least 30–50% of price), with separate regimes for fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims. | **Reject as sole cap; increase general cap.** A$4.8m is inadequate against a A$24m acquisition and cannot be used to cap specialist risks. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | A$25k de minimis; A$250k deductible basket; recovery only above basket. | Lower de minimis and a tipping/first-dollar basket, preferably A$10k / A$100k–150k. | **Counter.** The proposed thresholds exclude meaningful SaaS operational claims and the deductible structure shifts the first A$250k of loss to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | All general claims must be notified within 18 months; Seller seeks to apply limitations to all claims. | At least 24 months for general warranties, with longer tailored periods for tax, IP, title, fundamental and indemnity claims. | **Counter.** Eighteen months may expire before annual-cycle, customer-contract and regulatory issues reasonably emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month period as general warranties. | Title/capacity claims capped at 100% of price (or uncapped for title fraud), with a substantially longer period, such as 6–7 years. | **Reject.** Buyer must have durable recourse if it does not receive clean title to all shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims; no express fraud carve-out is provided. | Express preservation of claims and remedies for fraud, fraudulent concealment, wilful misconduct and intentional misrepresentation, including against relevant Seller persons. | **Add express carve-out.** Seller should not be able to rely on contractual limitations to protect deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Deems all matters in or referred to in the data room, Accounts, registers and public records disclosed generally. | Disclosure only where specific, fairly disclosed against the relevant warranty, and sufficiently detailed to identify nature and likely consequences; no blanket data-room/public-record disclosure. | **Reject blanket disclosure.** Data dumping and constructive disclosure deprive Buyer of the benefit of the warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from data room/public records. | Bar only claims based on actual knowledge of nominated senior Buyer deal-team members before signing, with no constructive knowledge or adviser knowledge attribution. | **Reject and narrow materially.** “Discoverable” knowledge and adviser attribution turn diligence materials into a broad warranty exclusion. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller says it will use reasonable endeavours and regards the matter as addressed by written consent; no final consent or satisfaction of conditions is in evidence. | Completion condition requiring written Bluefen consent, with all conditions satisfied or waived on terms acceptable to Buyer; termination/right to defer if absent. | **Make a hard CP.** Bluefen represents about A$3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue, so loss or impairment of the account is material. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately A$3.2m remains outstanding; release/security discharge may be provided after Completion. | Repayment at Completion from Seller proceeds, simultaneous lender payoff letter and discharge/release of all security and guarantees; no deduction from the agreed debt-free/cash-free price. | **Require closing deliverables, not a post-Completion promise.** Buyer must acquire the Company debt-free and free of Riverlark security at Completion. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | A$420k conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from funds flow and treated as Seller’s matter; on-costs are unstated. | Seller-funded payment at/before Completion or a purchase-price reduction/escrow, covering bonus, payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with an indemnity. | **Resolve expressly in funds flow.** These are Completion-triggered liabilities that could otherwise become a Company cost immediately after acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment issue only; A$180k remains open and no payment receipt or assignment confirmation is available. | Specific indemnity for all loss arising from Ironquay/SOW3, including ownership, infringement, assignment, payment and remediation risk; obtain payment evidence and confirmatory assignment before Completion. | **Expand indemnity and require evidence/CP.** Buyer needs assured ownership of the relevant project materials, not merely recourse for one invoice. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary incident; Seller does not accept confirmed breach, access, notification obligation or quantified loss. | Pre-Completion investigation and containment, full reporting, remediation and notification plan approved by Buyer, plus standalone uncapped/appropriately ring-fenced indemnity and warranty bring-down. | **Treat as a specific risk, not immaterial disclosure.** Affected personal information and uncertain access/notification exposure may create regulatory and customer consequences. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three A$110k renewals (A$330k total) are said to be ordinary-course operating costs; disclosure does not establish avoidability, timing or accrual. | Full contract details and confirmation of termination/renewal rights; prohibit renewal, prepayment or commitment outside agreed ordinary course without Buyer consent; adjust price if pre-Completion liabilities are excluded from working capital. | **Keep open pending facts.** “Ordinary course” does not establish that the commitments are avoidable, properly accrued or economically reflected in price. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions applying to all claims of every nature. | Express separation: general warranty regime must not limit claims under tax covenant, specific indemnities, Completion covenants, debt/cash adjustment, title/fundamental warranties, fraud or equitable/statutory remedies. | **Reject universal application.** A single limitation regime would improperly collapse negotiated, risk-specific Buyer protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%; says this is the source relied upon. | Up-to-date ASIC/company searches, register and certificates, board approvals, signed transfer instruments, release of all encumbrances/options and a clean title warranty. | **Require independent verification and closing evidence.** The register alone does not establish absence of liens, competing rights or defects in transferability. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP positions are settled under the general cap, basket and time-limit regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity (normally with tax-statute limitation period and no general basket/cap) and enhanced IP warranties/indemnities with tailored cap and survival. | **Reject.** Historic tax and IP ownership/infringement risks are not appropriately protected by the general warranty limitations. |
=== END ADVICE ===
